director.question: q0
director.why: q0 has the highest expected information at 0.145 bits and directly separates the rising Ia from the flat II plateau within three days.

question.text: Brighter in r three days from now than at its last r detection?

payload.rule: Every ZTF g or r measurement taken after this bet was sealed, up to one day past its last forecast, is scored against the forecast, interpolated linearly between days. The question is settled by the first r measurement within a day of its time; a limit above the reference leaves it void.

instrument.why: Coherent g and r detections persist over ~6 days at stable ~20 mag with good physical fits and a clean real stamp showing no subtraction residuals.

implausible.why: Fitted T=10000 K implying g-r~0.5 mag red colour is far cooler/redder than the hot blue (~20000-50000 K) continuum defining a TDE.

theories.argument: The six-day run of faint ~20 mag g and r detections after weeks of deeper limits is well fit by a z=0.0344 Type II template with chi2 per point 0.62 and leading weight 0.48. The roughly flat flux near 30 uJy in g and 36-48 uJy in r with a real isolated stamp (p_real 0.82) matches a faint Type II plateau rather than noise flicker.

refuted_if.why: A Type II plateau should stay nearly flat for weeks so a drop from near 36 uJy to below 18 uJy in five days is far too fast for hydrogen recombination

theories.weakest_point: The inferred rise and peak at day -14.6 fall in a ~5-day coverage gap with only shallow limits, so the peak brightness and plateau onset are extrapolated from only ~6 days of faint detections with lar

theories.argument: The last week of g near 20.1-20.3 and r near 19.7-20.0 detections after deep non-detections is well fit by a broad Type Ia (x1=2.7) rising to peak at day +0.8 with chi2 per point=0.73. The g-r near 0.3 mag color with c=0.29 matches a slightly reddened Ia on the rise, and the isolated round difference source (p_real=0.82) is consistent with a new transient.

refuted_if.why: The Ia fit predicts brightening to peak at +0.8 days so g should stay at or above the current near 32 uJy level near maximum, so a drop below 22 uJy would exclude the predicted rise.

theories.weakest_point: At z=0.0051 the near 20 mag detections imply M near -12 mag, about 7 mag too faint for a broad x1=2.7 Ia with only c=0.29 reddening, and g has stayed flat for about 6 days rather than rising steeply t

theories.argument: The six-day near-flat light curve at g ~20.2 mag and r ~19.7-20.0 mag with red g-r color matches a stripped-envelope supernova settling onto its 56Co tail at z=0.1636 with chi2 per point of 0.74. Pre-detection limits near 20.5 mag until day -20 and shallower 19-19.7 mag limits thereafter are consistent with a peak near day -21.6 fading into the currently observed tail brightness.

refuted_if.why: By 26 days after peak a Type Ibc must be declining on the 56Co tail, so sustained brightness near the current level would require a plateau power source incompatible with a stripped envelope.

theories.weakest_point: The entire rise, peak and fast early decline are unobserved and forced to hide in the sparsely sampled -21 to -12 day gap, so the peak luminosity and explosion date rest only on shallow limits.

wording.text: It is about as likely as not that the object will be brighter three days from now than at its last brightness measurement.
